There was a woman who was beautiful, who started with every advantage, and yet she had no luck, for she had married for love, and the love had turned to dust. <break time="0.8s" /> She had lovely children, yet she felt that they had been thrust upon her, and whenever they were near, she felt the center of her heart go hard. <break time="0.8s" /> Everybody said of her, She is such a good mother, and she adores her children, but only she herself and her children knew that it was not so. <break time="0.8s" /> They lived in a pleasant house with a garden and discreet servants, and they felt themselves superior to anyone in the neighborhood, yet there was never enough money. <break time="0.8s" /> The mother had a small income and the father had a small income, but it was not nearly enough for the social position which they had to keep up. <break time="0.8s" /> The father went into town to some office, but though he had good prospects, these prospects never materialized, and the mother, who tried this thing and the other, never succeeded either. <break time="0.8s" /> And so the house came to be haunted by an unspoken phrase, There must be more money, There must be more money, though nobody ever said it aloud. <break time="0.8s" /> The children could hear it all the time, especially at Christmas, when the expensive toys filled the nursery, and even the big rocking horse behind the smart dolls house seemed to hear it.
